scope:
Compare stable FP32 softmax formulations on identical observed TT scores.

Native PJRT execution with explicit non-dry-run options. IR is dumped by the
native compiler; codegen is never invoked. Operator timings include output D2H
from resident inputs and are not whole-attention/pipeline speed measurements.
finding: Unfused stable exp times reciprocal of exp sum reduces self/cross softmax error from 3.99%/2.36% to 0.0631%/0.0255%, about 63x/93x. All ten accepted cases repeat exactly with no fallback. Renormalizing native softmax is insufficient. Direct exp/div is fused back to native softmax; explicit reciprocal multiplication avoids the DivOp fusion pattern.
rejected: exp2 used aten::exp2 CPU fallback and is not a Tensix candidate. Initial ten-case grid hit Dynamo specialization limit; fresh compile cache per independent operator case completes fullgraph capture without changing sampler recompile gates.

observations: Matching Metal ComputeKernelConfig defaults math_approx_mode=true. Runtime sets it only when present; original softmax IR does not specify it.
Matching softmax program factory maps math_approx_mode to EXP_APPROX. This suggests approximate exponential math contributes, but configuration-toggle causality has not been tested.
TTIR SoftmaxFusionPattern matches DivOp(exp,reduce_sum(exp)); native IR confirms direct division fuses and reciprocal multiplication does not.

limit: Identical observed FP32 score tensors from synthetic learned attention. Not a full-flow or reconstruction-quality result. Newton reciprocal refinement adds no material improvement. Native IR dumped directly from ordinary non-dry-run PJRT; no codegen backend mutation.
next: Evaluate FP32 attention with the unfused reciprocal softmax in complete pretrained flows, including strict stock references, original trajectories, timing and decoded quality.
tests: 10 CPU checks cover stable formulations on aligned/unaligned widths and large offsets. All accepted hardware cases are finite, bitwise repeatable and fallback-free.
